info.bio: Jefferson Airplane fue una banda de Estados Unidos surgida en la ciudad de San Francisco (California), pionera del movimiento psicodélico influenciado por el LSD. Fue una de las primeras bandas de la escena de San Francisco en gozar de éxito comercial y crítico.  Su disco de 1967, Surrealistic Pillow, sigue siendo considerado como una de las principales obras del llamado "Verano del Amor", y trajo el reconocimiento internacional del grupo. Fue el segundo disco de la banda y el primero en incluir a la cantante

scenes.name: San Francisco: Acid Tests y Haight-Ashbury
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: A principios de 1966 había distritos psicodélicos con locales, grupos, ropa, impresos y drogas propios en Londres, Los Ángeles y San Francisco. Los Merry Pranksters de Ken Kesey convirtieron su desafío «Can You Pass the Acid Test?» en fiestas de luces, cine y sonido grabado y devuelto al instante: la segunda, en San José en diciembre de 1965 tras un concierto de los Stones, y nueve más en los tres primeros meses de 1966 (cinco en Los Ángeles, una en Watts). Los beats se habían mudado de North Beach a Haight-Ashbury; los Thelin abrieron la Psychedelic Shop y con Stewart Brand se hizo el Trips Festival (6.000 personas). La banda sonora era Rubber Soul. El caos sustituía al cuidado de Leary por el «set and setting»: en el Acid Test de Watts, Ken Babbs amplificó por micrófono los gritos de una chica en pleno mal viaje.

scenes.name: Alicia, la locura y el regreso a la infancia
scenes.author: Jon Savage
scenes.desc: Al final de 1966 el LSD llevó al pop de vuelta a la infancia y a la locura. Los Beatles empezaron el 24 de noviembre «Strawberry Fields Forever», un viaje de Lennon hacia abajo, no hacia atrás, al orfanato junto a su casa, «psicoanálisis con música», unida por Geoff Emerick a partir de dos tomas; luego «When I’m Sixty-Four» y «Penny Lane». En Navidad la BBC aplazó el Alice in Wonderland de Jonathan Miller, sin cabezas de animal, con el sitar de Ravi Shankar y rodado en un hospital militar de víctimas de neurosis de guerra: un catálogo de psicosis. Grace Slick llevó «White Rabbit» a Jefferson Airplane; Syd Barrett escribía sobre el mundo de Lewis Carroll. Proliferaban los discos sobre la locura («They’re Coming to Take Me Away, Ha-Haaa!», «Pandora’s Golden Heebie Jeebies» de los Association), y en el corazón secreto del año, la tristeza frágil de «How Can We Hang On to a Dream» de Tim Hardin.

scenes.name: Psicodelia y acid-rock
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En 1965 San Francisco se convierte en la ciudad más efervescente del país: los Grateful Dead tocan en los «acid tests» de Ken Kesey, nace la escena hippy y en 1966-67 llega el verano del amor. El acid-rock, evolución del folk-rock pensada como banda sonora del viaje de LSD, es el equivalente rockero de la pintura abstracta, el free jazz y la poesía beat: su gran invento es la «jam», con la guitarra eléctrica al mando y un espíritu zen en lugar del dolor del blues. Jefferson Airplane encarnan la era; los Grateful Dead inventan la improvisación colectiva libre (Anthem Of The Sun, Live Dead); Kaleidoscope, Moby Grape, Quicksilver, Blue Cheer o Fifty Foot Hose amplían el abanico. Monterey y Sgt Pepper (1967) convierten lo alternativo en mainstream. Fuera de California, Jimi Hendrix declara la guerra a la armonía occidental con su guitarra.

podcast.title: Chart Comparison for Aretha Franklin (1967)
podcast.body: Jefferson Airplane's LPs were among those sandwiching Aretha Franklin's Atlantic debut LP, "I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You," which climbed to number two on the Billboard album chart and stayed there for three weeks in 1967. This illustrates the diverse musical acts succeeding on the album charts during that period. "Her LP, I Never Loved a Man the Way I Love You, climbed to number two on the Billboard album chart and stayed there three weeks, sandwiched between LPs by the monkeys, the mamas and the poppas and the Jefferson airplane."

podcast.title: Personnel Shifts and Transition to Jefferson Starship (By 1974)
podcast.body: By 1974, the band had undergone "many shifts in personnel" and evolved into Jefferson Starship. A key reason for founding member Marty Balin's departure was his bandmates' "copious amounts of cocaine" and his desire for a different musical direction, explicitly not the "psychedelic experience." "By 1974 Jefferson airplane had undergone many shifts in personnel again one would require a flow chart and it became Jefferson's starship minus however one of the band's founders Marty Ballon in fact one reason that Marty Ballon left was because of the copious amounts of cocaine that his band my manbades were doing another was that he wanted to go in a different musical direction he was not so much into the psychedelic experience."

podcast.title: Musical Evolution and "Phase" (1975)
podcast.body: Paul Kantner stated in 1975 that the band considered their 1960s music a "phase" they "simply grew out of," signifying their deliberate shift in musical direction towards Jefferson Starship. "Paul Cantner was asked in 1975 about the musical changes in his band which had formed a decade earlier in San Francisco he said that the music that they made in the 60s was a phase that they simply grew out of."

xref.body: The Dukes of Stratosphear was XTC's pseudonymous project, conceived in 1985 to indulge their fascination with 1960s psychedelia. They adopted fake names for all band members and their producer, allowing them to experiment with a retro sound inspired by bands like Pink Floyd, The Byrds, Jefferson Airplane, Revolver-era Beatles, and The Beach Boys, purely for enjoyment and a break from their serious pop songs. "XTC wanted to try something a little retro, stuff that was outside their normal post-punk quirkiness."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: If That Is Your REAL Name

xref.title: All-Female San Francisco Group
xref.body: Ace of Cups was an all-female group formed in San Francisco in 1967, featuring Diane Metilige on drums. They were noted for opening for Jimi Hendrix and maintaining friendships with prominent bands like Jefferson Airplane and The Grateful Dead, marking their presence in the late 1960s psychedelic rock scene. "They were at all-female group formed in 1967 and featured die-end metallige on drums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Driven By Her: History of Female Drummers

xref.title: Associated with Influential Bay Area Bands
xref.body: The band were friends with other prominent San Francisco bands of the era, including the Grateful Dead and the Jefferson Airplane, demonstrating their integration into the vibrant local music scene. "They were also friends with the great full dead in the Jefferson Airplane and the guys in the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

xref.title: Formation and Early Connections
xref.body: Formed in San Francisco in 1967, coinciding with the Summer of Love, Ace of Cups consisted of five women without any male members. They were friends with The Grateful Dead and Jefferson Airplane, and Jimi Hendrix was so impressed that he invited them to open one of his gigs at Golden Gate Park. "They were formed in San Francisco in 1967, right in time for the summer of love."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Hidden Figures

xref.title: Musical Likes and Dislikes
xref.body: Green Day members indicated that they perceive themselves as carrying on the tradition of bands like The Ramones. They also identified groups such as Journey and Jefferson Airplane as examples of what they explicitly do not want to sound like, suggesting their identity is strongly shaped by their musical aversions. "And we like the remodels. That's what we're carrying on. This is it. We pretty much know who we don't want to sound like."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
